questions.original_semantic_description: A library management system includes entities such as Book, Author, and Member. The Book entity has attributes like ISBN, Title, and PublishYear. Each Author can write multiple Books, and a single Book can be written by one or more Authors. Members can borrow Books, and each Member can borrow multiple Books at a time. Each Member has a MembershipID and Name, while each Book has a specific ISBN.

questions.text: Consider a relation R(EmployeeID, EmployeeName, DepartmentID, DepartmentName) with the following set of functional dependencies F over R: F = {EmployeeID -> EmployeeName, DepartmentID -> DepartmentName, EmployeeID -> DepartmentID}.

subquestions.label: a
subquestions.text: Draw the functional dependency diagram.

subquestions.label: b
subquestions.text: Use the attribute closure and identify the primary key for the given relation.

subquestions.label: c
subquestions.text: If we insert a row <E123, John Doe, D1, null> into the given relation, what is the update anomaly that is violated? Give reasons.

subquestions.label: d
subquestions.text: Assume that the relation has a row, <E124, Jane Smith, D2, Logistics>. If we remove the department D2, what is the possible update anomaly that can be violated? Give reasons.

subquestions.label: e
subquestions.text: Using the above functional dependencies, design a set of 3NF relations for the above given relation. Show clearly each stage in deriving the 3NF relations. Also identify the normal form at each of these stages.

subquestions.label: f
subquestions.text: Do the update anomalies of part (c) and (d) hold in the 3NF relations? Discuss briefly.

subquestions.label: g
subquestions.text: Are the 3NF relations derived in part (e) still in 3NF? Justify your answer.

subquestions.label: h
subquestions.text: Are the 3NF relations derived in part (e) in BCNF? If not, bring the relations to BCNF.

questions.text:
Consider the following relational database schema containing details about a library system. In this system, the book relation stores information about different books, the member relation holds details about library members, the transaction relation records borrowings and returns, and the author relation contains information about book authors.

book (bid, title, genre, author_id)
member (mid, name, email, phone)
transaction (tid, mid, bid, date, status)
author (author_id, author_name, country)

subquestions.label: a
subquestions.text: Find the titles of books that have been borrowed at least once.

subquestions.label: b
subquestions.text: Identify the members who have never borrowed any books from the library.

subquestions.label: c
subquestions.text: Get the details of authors who have written books in the 'Science Fiction' genre.

subquestions.label: d
subquestions.text: Retrieve the names of members who have borrowed books by a specific author_id.

subquestions.label: e
subquestions.text: How many books are currently available (not borrowed)?

subquestions.label: f
subquestions.text: Express the above queries (a) to (d) in tuple calculus.
